title: Revolutionary Money-Saving Hack (MUST-HAVE for ALL Lifters!)
summary: His cheap substitute for dumbbells: loop a rope through a weight plate's hole and use it as a handle. He covers cost, space, joint-friendliness and gym use, demonstrates overhead triceps extensions, curls, rows and raises, shows how to combine the rope with a band anchored to a rack to mimic cables, and gives rope buying and knotting tips.
claims: Build a home gym gradually: pull-up bar, small rack or stands, an Olympic bar, then plates
With only a barbell you will struggle to isolate small muscles and risk a spider physique
Cheap second-hand dumbbells feel terrible, can cause wrist tendonitis and still cost $30-50 a pair
A rope looped through a plate replaces a dumbbell at 5-10 times lower cost, about $3-10
Rope loading needs no collars or clamps, takes any plate size or a kettlebell, and stores in almost no space
The rope lets you change wrist and hand angle freely, so it is easier on joints and tendons than steel dumbbells for curls; good for high-frequency arm work
In a commercial gym bring your own rope so you can run giant sets without hogging dumbbells
Rope-plate lifts are harder: 25 lb on a rope does the job of 40-50 lb on a dumbbell
The classic French press gave him bad triceps tendonitis; overhead extensions with a plate on a rope are easy on the tendon, and he now alternates the two
For small-muscle isolation drop the big-mover mindset; seated concentration curls with 25 lb already go a long way
Presses are awkward with a rope; do pressing compounds with a barbell
Do your standard barbell rows first, then rope-plate rows for higher reps with a short grip, a big stretch and an exaggerated squeeze
Grip close to the plate for a dumbbell feel (lateral raises), looser for upright rows
Tie a band to a rack and loop the rope through it to mimic a cable attachment for triceps extensions, rows or face pulls; it fixes the band's poor grip and the rope's dependence on gravity
Buy quality rope, about 10 ft for around $10, half an inch to an inch thick, cut into short and long pieces
Tie a knot at both ends of each rope as a safety stop so the hands can't slip off

let the weight hang behind, point elbows to favor the triceps; seated or standing

grip short, use the rope as the weight's extension; seated concentration style
freedom of wrist angle prevents tendonitis
shorten the rope, big stretch, exaggerated squeeze, higher reps
